Plan Matrix

Lay out a role plan as duties against time marks, every cell a proposal the reader can edit, with how they would know it is working at each mark.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Source lineSmall, secondary: where the rows come from and that every cell is a proposaltext-secondary
2NoteOptional, small, secondary: one caveat that changes how to read the plantext-secondary
3TableDuty column semibold (28%), one column per horizon; body 0.9375rem; hairline rowstext, border
4Horizon headersBy day N, one per horizon, from data (any count, any values)text-secondary
5Know stripOne cell per horizon: a mono label and one sentence on how the reader would know it is workingsurface, border, label cyan
6Phone rowsBelow 600px each row stacks: the duty, then each mark with its horizon as a labeltext-secondary labels

Usage

Use it when

  • A page proposes what someone will do by when, and the reader should be able to edit it.
  • The rows come from the reader’s own document (a job page, an RFP, a statement of work).

Do not use it when

  • A schedule with dependencies or dates; use a timeline.
  • More than five horizons; the columns stop reading on a laptop.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
horizons[]numbersyesDay marks, one column each, for example 30, 90, 180.
rows[][]stringsyesEach row: the duty, then one cell per horizon.
know[]stringsyesOne sentence per horizon.
source, notestringsnoWhere the rows come from; one caveat.

Access

  • A real <table> with <th> column headers; screen readers read each cell with its horizon.
  • On phones the header row hides and each mark carries its horizon as visible text (data-label), so nothing depends on position.
  • Static: no interaction, nothing hidden, prints whole.
